title: Cardinals, wide receiver Michael Wilson agree to 3-year, $75 million extension
content:
The Arizona Cardinals reached an agreement Thursday with wide receiver Michael Wilson on a three-year, $75 million contract extension, with $40 million guaranteed, according to his agency, Athletes First.

Wilson is preparing to play in the final year of his rookie contract. He was a third-round pick in 2023, the first draft for Monti Ossenfort as Cardinals GM.

“Monti and the Cardinals wanted to lock up a really good football player for as long as we could, and at the same time, the player wants the insurance and the security that he’s got a long-term deal,” Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said during his Thursday press conference.  “So it was both sides (that) wanted to get this done and got it done. …

“It’s great for (Wilson’s) teammates, this locker room. It’s good for the fan base. Anyone that really knows Mike, you can’t help but root for the guy. So that’s awesome.”

The 26-year-old Wilson led Cardinals receivers last year with 78 receptions, 1,006 yards and seven touchdowns.

This story will be updated.
